bear.story: AI optics cycle turns: hyperscaler capex growth slows faster than expected (Goldman sees +12% in 2028), EML/InP supply catches up (Coherent, Broadcom, Japanese and Chinese entrants), gross margin falls from ~50% toward the low 40s, FY28 EPS lands ~$24-26 instead of $33, and the multiple compresses to ~21-22x, near the bottom of the peer range (AVGO 20.5x, FN 25.5x). The JDSU 2001 bust is the extreme tail; a 2027 recession accelerates it.

base.story: Consensus is roughly met (FY28 ~$33, NTM ~$34 at horizon), CPO/OCS ramps, net cash builds; the multiple de-rates from ~50x FY27 / ~33x FY28 today to ~31-33x NTM as growth slows, so EPS growth is mostly offset by multiple compression, in line with the base rate that 5x winners earn about market returns afterwards.

bull.story: Management's ~$40 2028 earnings power proves conservative (NTM ~$45 at horizon), 1.6T EMLs stay supply-constrained, CPO and OCS add a second engine, and LITE holds ~40x, around the AI-connectivity peer median (ANET 44.6x, MRVL 49.9x). ~30% of 5x winners go on to another big multiple per Bessembinder.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$600 (about 18x FY28 consensus of ~$33, under the lowest peer forward P/E of 20.5x, and well under the July 2026 no-news panic low of ~$720), the price would most likely reflect a real break: a guidance cut, gross-margin reversal as EML supply catches up, a capex pause at one of the two customers that make up 42% of revenue, or share loss in transceivers/CPO, not ordinary 97%-vol noise. Raised from $560 because the corrected EPS base is higher.

reasoning: Lane: base rates. Round 2 corrects my earnings base: the $16.67 FY27 consensus I used was stale; the Q1 guide alone is $4.20, current consensus is ~$19.8-21.8 FY27 and ~$33 FY28 (MarketBeat, StockAnalysis), and the CEO has talked of ~$40 for 2028. NTM EPS at the horizon is therefore ~$34, not $28. I add ~$1.1B net cash (~$10.7/sh) and use ~103M shares, per the supervisor's 10-K reconciliation. The supervisor rightly said LITE's 5-year average P/E (31x) is a weak anchor, so I now set the multiple off 11 listed peers (median forward P/E 37.7x, range 20.5-62.4x; median forward EV/EBITDA ~28x). I apply an ~18% discount for reasons that persist through the horizon: higher cyclicality, scarcity-driven margins, customer concentration and weaker FCF conversion. That gives a P/E leg of $1,065, an EV/EBITDA cross-check of $1,070 and a base-rate anchor of $1,140; blended fair value is ~$1,085 (round 1: $990). My base-rate evidence still argues for a wide, roughly centred distribution: 5x winners show ~zero market-adjusted follow-on returns, but ~30% repeat; optical busts (JDSU 2001: revenue -66%, stock -98%) make the left tail fat, and LITE fell 33-43% in July 2026 on no news. I centre the ladder at a median of ~$1,060, slightly below fair value for the left skew, with log-sigma ~0.68 (below the trailing 97% realized vol, since vol after a parabolic year tends to mean-revert) and a slightly fatter left tail: P(>= spot) 0.485 (round 1: 0.455), P(>= $543) 0.825, P(>= $2,714) 0.075. The Kalshi recession figure is no longer used numerically. comps_summary.peer_median_growth_next_yr: revenue ~+50% (mixed fiscal years; see each peer)
comps_summary.lite_today: Today LITE trades at 49.8x forward (FY27) P/E and ~36x derived forward EV/EBITDA (StockAnalysis), a ~32% P/E premium to the peer median, backed by +110% FY27 revenue and +151% EPS growth, well above every peer except AAOI.
comps_summary.lite_in_my_methods: My P/E leg uses 31x NTM-at-horizon EPS (~18% below the 37.7x peer median, inside the range) and my EV/EBITDA leg uses 23x (~18% below the 28.1x median, inside the range).
comps_summary.justification: The discount applies at the horizon, when LITE's growth will have slowed toward the peer pace (FY28 consensus +~67%, then mid-teens to 30% into FY29 as Goldman sees hyperscaler capex growth slowing to ~12% in 2028), so growth no longer earns the premium it earns today. Four traits should persist through the horizon. (1) Cyclicality. LITE is a component maker whose earnings swing with one end market: its own forward P/E has ranged 10-54x, and the closest historical analogue (JDSU 2001) lost two thirds of its revenue in a year. That makes it more like FN (25.5x) and COHR (35.8x) than like the diversified or platform peers (APH, ANET, AVGO, MRVL). (2) Margin quality. Gross margin rose from ~33% to ~50% on EML/InP scarcity pricing, and Coherent, Broadcom and Chinese entrants are adding capacity. Peers like CRDO and ALAB (~67% GM) and ANET have structurally higher margins. (3) Concentration. Two customers were 42% of FY26 revenue, with 26.6% from Hong Kong and China. (4) Returns and cash. FY26 FCF was only ~$300M (OCF $751M less capex $451M), so ROIC and FCF conversion lag the asset-light peers. Against this, LITE's balance sheet (~$1.1B net cash) and ~40% operating margin are at or above most of the peers, so I do not push to the bottom of the range. An ~18% discount puts LITE between the hardware-optics subset (COHR, CIEN, FN, AAOI; median ~36.7x) and the cyclical floor. I use no sell-side outperformance call. The peer EV/EBITDA figures are my own derivation from forward P/E (cross-checked against COHR's cited consensus EBITDA) and carry ~10% error.
